issue: prereg.sh audit's DATA check fails for all four vendor/ms/{ms.c,streec.c,rand1.c,ms.h} entries in the frozen prereg's '## Frozen data checksums' section, reported as 'missing' for each file. Two independent format mismatches, both inherited from the pre-freeze draft (not introduced by the round-2 red-team edit or by the freeze itself): (1) the checksum lines are written as '- `path` — `hash`' (backticked path, em-dash separator, backticked hash); the script's awk parser expects the bare '- path hash' format it itself emits when `prereg.sh freeze <file> <data...>` generates this section automatically, so splitting on whitespace, field 2 comes out as '`vendor/ms/ms.c`' (backticks included) and field 3 as the em-dash, never reaching the hash. (2) even with the format fixed, the recorded values are plain SHA-256 (64 hex chars, via `shasum -a 256`, matching how the plan's own §0.2/R1 checksums were produced) while the script's DATA check compares against `git hash-object` (git's blob hash — a different algorithm and length); this section was hand-authored into the document during drafting rather than produced by passing these files as freeze-time data args, so it was never going to be audit-parseable by this mechanism regardless of format.
correction: verified by hand instead, post-freeze, without editing the frozen file (an edit would itself fail INTEGRITY): `shasum -a 256 vendor/ms/{ms.c,streec.c,rand1.c,ms.h}` in ~/Projects/newlife, run 2026-08-31, reproduced all four hashes recorded in the frozen prereg's checksums section exactly. The vendored ms sources have not drifted or been tampered with since drafting; the substantive DATA question the check exists to answer is independently confirmed 'yes'. `prereg.sh audit`'s automated DATA arm will report FAIL for this preregistration indefinitely — a known, understood gap in that arm for this specific file, not evidence of an actual data-integrity problem. Future preregistrations that record raw-data checksums by hand, rather than via `prereg.sh freeze <file> <data...>`'s own generation path, should either use that generation path or note in the document that the DATA arm of `prereg.sh audit` will not verify them.

issue: R3's justification for `ca()`'s swap-with-last chromosome bookkeeping ('valid because with one segment tseg never goes negative so the fully absorbed branch never triggers', frozen prereg R3 / plan §3) is imprecise. Verified by reading vendor/ms/streec.c's `ca()` while implementing Task 1's Python port: `tseg` DOES go negative, on every replicate, on the final coalescent event (the merge that creates the root). `nnodes[seg]` reaches exactly `2*nsam-2` (the root's node index) on that merge, which triggers `if(nnodes[seg]>=(2*nsam-2)) tseg--;` (streec.c ~line 608), taking `tseg` from 0 to -1 and routing execution into the `if(tseg<0)` branch (streec.c ~line 629) that R3's prose claims is unreachable.
correction: this does not affect correctness of R3's algorithm or Task 1's port, and required no code change. Both the `tseg<0` and `tseg>=0` branches of `ca()` set the two merging nodes' `abv` fields and the new node's `time` field unconditionally and identically (streec.c ~lines 606-617, before the tseg-dependent branch). The only thing that differs between the branches is internal `chrom[]`/`nchrom` slot bookkeeping (which array slot gets recycled from the end, and whether `nchrom` decrements once or twice on the final merge) -- pure implementation detail of ms's own array-reuse strategy, never observable in printed output (segsites count, genotype matrix) or in draw consumption. The Python port's simplified `active`-list model (`active[c1]=new_node; active[c2]=active[-1]; active.pop()`) does not replicate this exact bookkeeping quirk, but produces an identical tree either way, which Task 1's real-`ms`-binary bit-for-bit test confirms directly (all 30 frozen-grid replicates pass exactly, including the final-merge event of every one of them). No change to R3's algorithm, the frozen grid, or any decision criterion; recorded because a future reader tracing the C source against R3's prose would otherwise trip on the same false lead the prose does.

issue: Task 2's checklist item for world.py (plan section, round-2 red-team addition) instructs: pack a literal -seeds triple into a single integer via R2's word order (X_0 = seedv[0]|seedv[1]<<16|seedv[2]<<32) and feed it through a `stream_factory`-style seeding path for the Task 1/2 cross-check, mirroring World 1's RngBank/stream_factory pattern. Implementing this literally does not, and cannot, make tier (b) (mechanism registry) reproduce tier (a)'s (standalone port) output. Re-seeding any PRNG from a packed integer -- even the correctly R2-packed literal triple -- produces a sequence of draws with zero relationship to ms's own drand48 stream: matching outputs requires consuming the *same float values* in the *same order*, not merely 'the same seed' fed to an unrelated generator.
correction: CoalescentWorld (world.py) takes an already-constructed draw-stream object directly (`draws` parameter), not a `stream_factory`/root_seed pair. For the Task 1/2 cross-check test (test_mechanism_registry.py), this is a RecordedDrawStream built from the same real ms draw log Task 1's own test built for that seed triple -- two independent stream instances loaded from the identical log, one consumed by run_replicate (tier a), one by CoalescentWorld (tier b), and all 30 replicates match exactly. This is not a deviation from the plan's actual requirement: R2's own frozen sentence already says the cross-check 'needs no seed derivation at all' -- only the later, round-2-added implementation hint about routing it through a packed-seed stream_factory was wrong about the mechanism. pack_ms_triple is still real, exercised code: it is used correctly by the separate, non-frozen-grid run_from_rng_bank requirement, where matching ms's output is explicitly not required and a re-seeded generator is exactly the right tool. No criterion changed -- both Task 2 checklist requirements pass; only the mechanism connecting them to the plan's stream_factory language was corrected during implementation.
